title: Adab of the road
hookLine: the companions want to keep sitting by the road, so they're told what the road is owed

lines: THEN GIVE THE ROAD ITS RIGHT.
cards: Do roads have rights? A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari says they do. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri reports that the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, told his companions to avoid sitting along the roads.
They pushed back. Those are our meeting places, they said. That's where we talk.
So he didn't argue. He said, in paraphrase: if you must sit there, then give the road its right. And they asked the obvious next question.

teach.h: A STREET OWES, AND IS OWED.
teach.b: His answer, in paraphrase: lowering the gaze, holding back harm, returning the greeting, and urging what is good while forbidding what is wrong.
A street belongs to no one in particular, and that doesn't make it a free-for-all. Everyone on it is owed something by everyone else. First, the eyes.
In al-Nur, in Pickthall's translation: "Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and be modest." The next verse says the same to the believing women.
On a crowded street, a lowered gaze is a kind of privacy for people who can't close a door. Second, harm.
Bukhari tells of a man who found a thorny branch lying across a road and moved it aside, and Allah thanked him for it and forgave him. One branch.
And in Sahih Muslim, faith has many branches, the highest the declaration that there is no god but Allah, the lowest removing something harmful from the road. Even the lowest branch is still faith.
Third, the greeting, from day three hundred eighty-four.
Al-Nisa, Pickthall again: "When ye are greeted with a greeting, greet ye with a better than it or return it." It's owed back, and better if you can.
And the last piece turns the sidewalk into a place where people look out for one another. The companions asked for permission to sit. What they got was a job.

how: Muslims cite the hadith of the road's rights when teaching public manners, and treat lowering the gaze, returning salam and removing harm from the path as acts of faith.

games.q: what does “adab of the road” mean?
o: what people owe each other in shared spaces
the traffic laws a Muslim country enforces
the rules for where a mosque may be built

games.q: the adab of the road — tap the pairs.
p: the road's right for the eyes
moved aside, and the man forgiven
return it, or a better one

s: the companions were simply forbidden to sit by the road
when they said they had no choice, he said: then give the road its right.
returning a greeting with a better one is in the Qur'an
al-Nisa: greet ye with a better than it or return it.
removing harm from the road is counted as a branch of faith
in Sahih Muslim, the lowest branch of faith is removing something harmful from the road.

games.q: you're walking along a road and a thorny branch lies across it. nobody's watching. what does the man in the hadith do?
o: step around it; someone else will move it.
move it out of the way.
complain about it to the first person he meets.
games.why: he moved the branch aside, and the hadith says Allah thanked him for it and forgave him. one branch.

practice: Picture the street, hallway or parking lot you'll pass through next, and the people on it.

Let your eyes come down gently where they don't need to wander, see your hand moving whatever's in the way, a bottle, a cart, a bag in the aisle, and hear yourself answering a greeting a little warmer than it came.
If you pray, you can return a salam with wa 'alaykum al-salam.

wordCard.voice: Adab of the road. The manners of shared space: lower the gaze, hold back harm and clear it away, return the greeting, and urge the good. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a right, a due; the road's haqq.

carryVoice: Your line: the road's rights. Even the lowest branch is still faith. See you at the market tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 6229 (Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: give the road its right)

sources.q: Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and be modest.

sources.ref: Qur'an 24:31 (the same to the believing women)
Sahih al-Bukhari 652 (the man who moved a thorny branch from the road)
Sahih Muslim 35 (the branches of faith; the lowest is removing harm from the road)

sources.q: When ye are greeted with a greeting, greet ye with a better than it or return it.
